items.title: PCRS and NHS Wales primary care respiratory update, Cardiff, 20 October 2026
items.summary: PCRS is running a one-day essential primary care respiratory update in Cardiff on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with NHS Wales Performance and Improvement and members of the National Respiratory Audit Programme. A concentrated Welsh primary care respiratory audience.

items.title: GP contract negotiations for 2027/28 to start next month, says BMA
items.summary: GP contract negotiations for the next financial year are due to start in November, the BMA’s GP committee has confirmed. In an update to LMCs, the GPC said that contract negotiations for 2027/28 are now due to start next month, after ‘further discussion’ with NHS England.

items.title: What does the Fonagy review into ADHD mean for GPs?
items.summary: Pulse takes an in-depth look at the recent independent review into ADHD and autism ‘Mental health conditions, ADHD and autism overlap in many people’s lives, but they differ in important ways: in how they arise, how they develop, how they affect day-to-day life, and how they are best understood and supported,’ says…

items.title: Five AI tools approved for identifying prostate cancer on MRI scans
items.summary: Five artificial intelligence tools for more accurately detecting prostate cancer in MRI scans have been approved for use on the NHS. NICE said the tools have the potential to act like a ‘second pair of eyes’, helping radiologists review prostate MRI scans and improve accuracy and consistency of diagnosis.

items.title: Joint GP and community pharmacy conference to return for 2027 in London
items.summary: GPs and community pharmacy professionals are invited to a free-to-attend conference in London next June which aims to bring the two groups together to collaborate as the Government aims to shift care out of hospital.

items.title: NHS 111 calls reduced following GP online access changes, CQC finds
items.summary: Calls to NHS 111 have been decreasing following GP online access changes and the launch of Pharmacy First, the CQC has said in its annual assessment of health and social care in England.

items.title: CQC flags ‘considerable’ regional variation in practice nurse workforce
items.summary: A shortage of practice nurses in some areas is increasing pressures for existing staff and reducing capacity to provide timely care, the healthcare watchdog has warned.

items.title: Community Pharmacy and General Practice Conference returns in 2027
items.summary: Primary care nursing professionals will have the opportunity to explore how closer working between general practice and community pharmacy can improve patient care at the second annual Community Pharmacy and General Practice Conference, which moves to London in 2027.

items.title: Falling immigration could put pressure on NHS finances, analysis warns
items.summary: The NHS has become increasingly reliant on revenue from the Immigration Health Surcharge (HIS) which generated almost £2.5bn in 2024/25, according to the Nuffield Trust.

items.title: MPs demand weight management overhaul amid ‘unambitious’ Mounjaro rollout
items.summary: NHS weight management care needs to be completely overhauled, say MPs who found poor access to a range of treatments, including drugs and surgery. The Health and Social Care Committee said obesity should be treated as a long-term, managed condition like diabetes.

items.title: Alzheimer’s trial launches to test diabetes and ADHD drugs
items.summary: A large UK study has been launched to test several drugs for Alzheimer’s disease that are already being used for other conditions. The multi-arm adaptive randomised controlled trial being run across 30 NHS sites when fully operational will initially test metformin and atomoxetine with results expected by 2030.

items.title: Clinical casebook: Common nail conditions
items.summary: In our latest CPD module, GPwER in dermatology Dr Chitra Nair discusses four cases involving common nail conditions and advises on their appropriate diagnosis and management. Complete the full module today and earn 2 CPD points.

items.title: Syncope as a clue to sarcoidosis
items.summary: Under the radar: GPSI in respiratory medicine Dr Andrew Powell describes how an episode of syncope led to a diagnosis of sarcoidosis, and the clues that can help GPs recognise this multisystem condition Note: details of the case in this article have been altered to ensure anonymity The case A 55-year-old woman…

items.title: Record 5,000 doctors secure GP training places as competition eases
items.summary: A record number of resident doctors secured GP training posts this year, the Government has announced.

items.title: Nursing students should spend half their placements in community settings, says QICN chief
items.summary: Nursing students should spend at least 50% of their clinical placement time in a community setting, including GP practices, care homes and schools, the chief executive of the Queens Institute of Community Nursing (QICN) has urged.

items.title: Beyond memory loss: recognising dementia in primary care
items.summary: An estimated one third of older people with dementia in England remain undiagnosed. Rachel Daly, academy lead Admiral Nurse at Dementia UK, explains how primary care nurses are well placed to recognise the patterns that point to the condition and make timely referrals. Dementia rarely presents as a direct concern.

items.title: First needle-free adrenaline treatment for young children launched in the UK
items.summary: The first needle-free adrenaline treatment for young children is now available in the UK. The 1mg nasal spray was launched on Tuesday (20 October) and is available for the emergency treatment of anaphylaxis in young children aged 4 years and over who weigh 15 kg to less than 30 kg. The announcement comes after the...

items.title: Government developing ‘national definition’ for delayed community care
items.summary: The government is working on a national definition for care that is postponed or delayed within the community, health minister Karin Smyth has said.

items.title: GPs urged to write to RCGP opposing physician associate protocol
items.summary: The BMA has encouraged GPs to write to the RCGP opposing a clinical protocol which would allow physician associates (PAs) to see undifferentiated patients in general practice under heavy supervision.

items.title: Government sets out detail of crackdown on cosmetic procedures
items.summary: The Government has set out proposals for limiting who can carry out high-risk cosmetic procedures such as liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), vampire facials and chemical peels.

items.title: GPs left chasing patients’ ‘disappeared’ hospital referrals in NHS safety failure
items.summary: GPs have been left chasing patients’ missing referrals after an NHS system removed them from hospital worklists without any warning, a damning safety investigation has revealed.

items.title: Unions and MPs warn that GP nurses will be ‘left behind’ on pay
items.summary: Calls by some ministers and unions to ringfence GP nursing salaries have gone unanswered by the government and NHS England despite their recommendation to boost pay for GPs and doctors.

items.title: I failed to bring back family doctors, says Jeremy Hunt
items.summary: Former health secretary Sir Jeremy Hunt said that he ‘tried and failed’ to bring back family doctors – and urged the Government to introduce ‘some changes in the next GP contract negotiations to bring back the system we used to have’.

items.title: It’s beginning to look a lot like charity
items.summary: Copperfield on how recently announced funding to GP practices in one area still falls short amid the wider financial doom and gloom in general practice It’s only October, but it must feel like Christmas to practices in Berks, Bucks and Oxfordshire.

items.title: ADHD linked to higher odds of early death, but medication may alleviate risk
items.summary: People with ADHD are more likely to die early than those without the condition, but taking the right medication might reduce this risk, a new study has found.

items.title: Nursing in Practice Podcast: Inside this year’s winter vaccination programme
items.summary: The latest episode of the Nursing in Practice Podcast welcomes two general practice nurses (GPNs) to discuss the latest trends, demands and challenges within this year’s winter vaccination programme.

items.title: NHSE reminds GPs of carcinogenic risk of some cancer treatments following patient death
items.summary: GPs should ‘be aware’ of the carcinogenic risk of some cancer treatments, NHS England has said following the death of a patient who had a rare radiation-induced cancer.

items.title: ICB may use Google reviews to check and manage GP practices’ performance
items.summary: Exclusive Google reviews may be used by one ICB to identify and manage the performance of GP practices with low patient satisfaction rates, Pulse has learnt.

items.title: Petition demands urgent action as graduate midwives still left without jobs
items.summary: The Royal College of Midwives (RCM) has launched a petition ‘demanding urgent action’ from the Welsh Government as more than 60 midwifery graduates are understood to still be without roles.

items.title: Nurses included in government crackdown on high-risk cosmetic treatments
items.summary: The government has announced plans to restrict the provision of high-risk cosmetic procedures to qualified healthcare professionals as part of a crackdown on unregulated practitioners carrying out potentially dangerous treatments.

items.title: Covid inquiry calls for care home visiting rights in future pandemics
items.summary: Care home residents should retain the right to receive visitors in person during future pandemics, except in the most serious or exceptional circumstances, the UK Covid-19 Inquiry has recommended.

items.title: CQC must be prepared to do on-site inspections in a future pandemic, Covid Inquiry says
items.summary: The CQC should develop a protocol for carrying out on-site inspections – as well as hybrid and remote – in a future public health emergency, the Covid Inquiry has recommended. The protocol should be guided by the ‘core principle’ of continuing on-site inspections ‘where possible’, the inquiry said.

items.title: Single patient record could remove need for patient consent to share GP data, BMA warns
items.summary: The proposed NHS single patient record risks removing requirements to seek patients’ consent to share GP data, the BMA has warned. The union urged peers in the House of Lords to amend the Health Bill to ensure the common law duty of confidentiality continues to apply to medical records.

items.title: Marketing authorisation for chikungunya vaccine withdrawn by MHRA
items.summary: The marketing authorisation for a chikungunya vaccine licensed for use in the UK has officially been withdrawn by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA).

items.title: Financial support scheme needed for care workers ahead of future pandemic
items.summary: A financial support scheme to protect care workers from losses resulted by mandatory self-isolation rules must be in place for a future pandemic, a national inquiry has urged.

items.title: Proposed 2.4% pay rise for NHS nurses a ‘betrayal’, say unions
items.summary: A proposed 2.4% pay uplift for NHS nurses for the next financial year has been dubbed a ‘betrayal’ and ‘derisory’ by unions. This week, the government announced its recommendation for the pay uplift for nurses working in general practice and the NHS.

items.title: Baroness Gerada: ‘The Health Bill must protect GP continuity of care’
items.summary: Practising GP and peer in the House of Lords Baroness Gerada of Kennington makes the case as to why continuity of care must be protected and resourced in the Health Bill My very first patient as a GP was a young woman who had just suffered a stillbirth.

items.title: Covid pandemic ‘exposed and exacerbated’ social care workforce ‘fragility’
items.summary: The Covid pandemic placed a stark lens on the ‘underlying fragility’ of the adult social care workforce and demonstrated how the sector has long been ‘undervalued and under-recognised’, a national inquiry has concluded.

items.title: NHS England to spend £80m on ‘multi-neighbourhood’ GP training hubs
items.summary: NHS England is inviting potential bidders for an £80m contract to create ‘multi-neighbourhood training hubs’ which will be ‘go-to’ points for training in general practice.

items.title: Newly-formed ICB apologises for delays in paying GP practices
items.summary: Exclusive A newly-formed ICB has apologised for delays in processing payments to GP practices, after the local LMC estimated they were owed on average around £50,000 in ‘outstanding payments’.

items.title: Concern as community care ‘left out’ of government’s winter funding plans
items.summary: The government has been urged to recognise the care being missed in people’s homes as part of its winter preparedness plans.

items.title: Nurse views sought on allowing schools to hold spare adrenaline nasal sprays
items.summary: A consultation has been launched on enabling schools to purchase and keep adrenaline nasal sprays for emergency use in children with severe allergies.

items.title: Government to explore linking GP and hospital records to monitor vaccine safety
items.summary: The Government has supported the Covid inquiry’s finding that GP and hospital records across the UK should be linked to monitor vaccine safety.

items.title: Vacancies found for nursing graduates left without jobs in Wales
items.summary: Vacancies have been found for nursing graduates in Wales who have been unemployed since qualifying this summer, it has been confirmed.

items.title: Government recommends 2.4% pay rise for nurses next year
items.summary: The government has planned for a 2.4% pay uplift for nurses working in general practice and the NHS for the next financial year. In its submission to the pay review bodies for general practice and NHS staff, the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and NHS England (NHSE) said that should a pay award...

items.title: Government planning for 2.4% GP pay rise next year, DDRB told
items.summary: The Government has told the independent doctors’ pay review body that it is currently planning for a pay uplift of 2.4% for GPs for the next financial year.

items.title: GP practices overlooked in Government £140m winter pressure boost
items.summary: The Government has announced £140m extra funding to address winter pressures, but none of this will be for general practice.

items.title: NHSE updates ‘patient charter’ rules for GP practices to include online access requirements
items.summary: NHS England has published a new version of its ‘patient charter’ document which practices have to follow and display on their websites, including a new section on online requests and clarifications on response times.

items.title: Plague: what do nurses need to know?
items.summary: Plague made headlines earlier this month after reports emerged that a laboratory worker in Russia had died, having possibly contracted the infectious disease in a workplace accident.

items.title: You and your general practice
What will the arrival of thousands of new pharmacist prescribers mean for general practice?
items.summary: This autumn sees the first cohort of pharmacists to graduate with prescribing powers. It means thousands more independent prescribers working in the community. Emma Wilkinson looks at the plans for NHS services and the safeguards being put in place. What has changed?

items.title: Women more likely to be told autoimmune symptoms are psychosomatic
items.summary: Women with autoimmune diseases are more likely to be told their symptoms are psychosomatic, research suggests. A study of sex differences in the diagnostic experiences of 6,607 people with autoimmune diseases also found that female patients were more likely to face delays in getting a correct diagnosis.

items.title: Your call is important to us. Your health? Not so much
items.summary: Copperfield on how an overstretched and impersonal NHS leaves GPs to pick up the pieces of all the patients lost in the system The stat that two thirds of patients contact their GP at least once a year because of delays with other NHS services actually understates the problem.

items.title: Hospital trust to divert £325,000 into GP practices to tackle underfunding
items.summary: GP practices in one area will receive money directly from a hospital trust to address underfunding and low patient satisfaction. Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust (BHT) has said it will transfer £325,000 to 12 GP practices initially as part of its ‘GP Capacity and Outcomes Fund’.

items.title: Nursing in Practice North event to explore managing complex wounds alongside skin conditions
items.summary: The overlap between skin conditions and wound care – and how to manage both alongside one another – will be explored at our Nursing in Practice North 2026 event next month.

items.title: GPs to advise about suicidal behaviour risks when prescribing antidepressants
items.summary: GPs should discuss the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours when starting or changing the dose of an antidepressant, the UK medicines regulator has said.

items.title: Counterfeit weight loss jabs worth £2m seized in Birmingham raid
items.summary: More than 12,000 counterfeit weight loss medicine jabs worth around £2m have been seized in a raid on an industrial unit in Birmingham.

items.title: Almost half with flu-like symptoms miss work or school, UKHSA finds
items.summary: Almost half of people in work or education who had flu-like symptoms took time off sick during recent winter seasons, according to new data from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

items.title: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust — Neighbourhood COPD Risk Stratification Project - PCN Collaboration (C484015)
items.summary:
Advances in COPD treatment and management provide an opportunity to improve outcomes through earlier identification and intervention using a risk-based approach to care, focused on identifying patients at greatest risk and providing timely access to specialist support and treatment.

This project  Responses by…

items.title: Mental health nurses to vote on strike action over alleged job cut plans
items.summary: Mental health nurses working at the East London NHS Foundation Trust (ELFT) are being asked to vote on taking strike action as part of a dispute centred on alleged plans to axe hundreds of jobs.

items.title: Managing hair loss – a practical guide for GPs
items.summary: GPwER in Dermatology Dr Anna Trigell outlines a practical guide to consultations about hair loss, including how to take a structured approach to diagnosis, what treatments to initiate in primary care and how to counsel patients Hair loss is a symptom that may be considered by clinicians as a benign condition, but for…

items.title: How not to miss: Scabies
items.summary: In the first of a new series looking at conditions that can easily be overlooked or misattributed, Dr Keith Hopcroft describes how a case of scabies is initially treated as eczema – and explores some of the other pitfalls that can lead to a delayed diagnosis of this contagious infection Note cases in this…

items.title: Immigration reform could put thousands of healthcare staff ‘at risk’
items.summary: Government plans for immigration reform could cost the NHS at least £169m and put the future of 12,000 healthcare workers in jeopardy, NHS Employers and Unison have warned.

items.title: ‘Advanced practice should mean advanced opportunity, not just advanced responsibility’
items.summary: Advanced clinical practitioner Jane Eastwood wants to see more training and opportunities for those working in primary care, arguing that advanced practice should provide advanced opportunity, not just advanced responsibility.

items.title: Dispensing GP practices should deliver pharmacy services in rural areas, report says
items.summary: Dispensing GP practices should be commissioned to deliver pharmacy services in rural areas, a new report has recommended.

items.title: District nursing at heart of Welsh Government’s winter NHS plans, minister says
items.summary: District nursing is central to the Welsh Government’s plans to ease winter pressures on hospitals by providing more care in the community, health minister Mabon ap Gwynfor has told the Senedd.

items.title: Pharmacy First-issued medicines increase by nearly a third
items.summary: Last year saw a substantial jump in the number of medicines issued through Pharmacy First clinical consultations, figures show.

items.title: Conjunctivitis: what nurses need to know
items.summary: Conjunctivitis is a common presentation that practice and community nurses will encounter. While many cases will resolve on their own, some patients need treatment and others require urgent referral.

items.title: Government announces £33m investment in dementia research initiative
items.summary: The government is to provide £33m of funding focused on recruitment for clinical studies to test new treatments for dementia. The investment will be made through the Dame Barbara Windsor Dementia Goals programme, alongside funding from Bristol Myers Squibb, GSK and Gates Ventures.

items.title: GPs in one area given £2m ‘premium’ to ‘support shift from hospital to community’
items.summary: One ICB has redesigned its ‘GP premium scheme’ to support the neighbourhood health model and a shift ‘away from hospital-based care’, backed by over £2m in funding for this financial year.

items.title: MHRA announces measures to improve messaging on antidepressant risks
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has announced a series of measures to strengthen messaging around the key risks associated with antidepressant medicines. New boxed warnings will carry information on suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and signpost where patients can get help.

items.title: Study links statin use with lower risk of glaucoma
items.summary: People taking statins may have a lower risk of developing glaucoma or needing more intensive treatment for the condition, new research suggests. A study, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology, found statin use was associated with a 15% lower risk of developing open-angle glaucoma.

items.title: CQC to regulate all diagnostic assessments for ADHD and autism
items.summary: The Government has asked the CQC to regulate all diagnostic assessments for autism and ADHD, once regulations are in place, following an independent review.

items.title: GPs given new legal duties to proactively share information for child safeguarding
items.summary: GPs are now legally required to proactively share information about children with other safeguarding organisations where there are concerns about their welfare, even if they are not yet at risk of harm.

items.title: ADHD care needs compassion as well as proper funding
items.summary: Editor Sofia Lind on the access and funding required by GPs to take on long-term ADHD management for patients, following the Government-commissioned independent review published last week A recent Pulse survey found that seven in 10 UK GPs believe ADHD is being overdiagnosed, with nearly half of all respondents saying…

items.title: RCN Council chair and vice chair re-elected
items.summary: The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has announced the re-election of the chair and vice chair of its governing council. Carmel O’Boyle has been re-elected as chair of RCN Council, the nursing union’s governing body.

items.title: Nurses in Northern Ireland balloted on strike action over ongoing pay dispute
items.summary: Nurses working in Northern Ireland’s Health and Social Care (HSC) service are being balloted on whether they want to take strike action over an ongoing pay dispute.

items.title: AI-written complaints harming GP staff wellbeing
items.summary: AI-generated complaints from patients are increasing workload and damaging GP practice teams’ wellbeing and morale, almost half of practice managers (45%) have reported in a survey.

items.title: HRT patches out of stock until end of November
items.summary: A brand of transdermal hormone replacement therapy (HRT) patch is out of stock, the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has announced.

items.title: ASA clamps down on rule-breaking pharmacy weight-loss medicine adverts
items.summary: The Advertising Standards Agency (ASA) has clamped down for the first time on online promotion of oral weight loss drugs. It found two online pharmacies had broken the rules by promoting unlicenced medicines and prescription-only medicines to the public in adverts for oral GLP-1 treatments.

items.title: GPs to lead neighbourhood health model with £8m fund repurposed from hospitals
items.summary: Exclusive One GP federation will lead the neighbourhood health model in its area, which has been allocated £8m of funding repurposed from hospital growth, Pulse has learnt.

items.title: Social care nurse turnover ‘shockingly high’
items.summary: The number of registered nurses working in adult social care in England has increased for the third consecutive year, while the vacancy rate has fallen, according to a new report from Skills for Care.

items.title: AI-generated patient complaints adding to GP practice workload, survey finds
items.summary: Almost half (45%) of GP practice managers say AI-generated patient complaints are increasing workloads and affecting staff wellbeing and morale, according to a survey by the Medical Protection Society. The poll of almost 160 UK practice managers found just 7% said they had not encountered an AI-generated complaint.

items.title: Once-weekly insulin jab for type 2 diabetes authorised by MHRA
items.summary: A new once-weekly insulin treatment for adults with type 2 diabetes has been authorised by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA). Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa) is a long-acting basal insulin that could cut the injections needed by patients currently on daily treatment from 365 a year to 52.

items.title: Visa changes spark fresh appeal from RCN to protect migrant nurses
items.summary: The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has once again urged the government to make further changes to visa rules to better protect migrant nursing staff as new changes come into effect.

items.title: Nursing academic wins award for ‘global impact’ on wound care practice
items.summary: A nursing academic has won an award for her work in improving wound care and promoting responsible antimicrobial use.

items.title: Can GPs improve ADHD care? And BMA chair on why physician associates should not diagnose patients
items.summary: The new episode of Pulse in Focus: The Podcast for GPs is now live and available on all podcast platforms. In this month’s episode, we look at what the landmark Government-commissioned review into ADHD means for general practice.

items.title: GP surgery closed amid car park rape investigation
items.summary: Detectives have arrested four men on suspicion of rape, after a woman in her 30s reported being sexually assaulted in Swindon last night. An ‘investigative scene’ is currently in place in the carpark of the Great Western Surgery in Farriers Close, Wiltshire Police told Pulse, and the surgery remains closed.

items.title: ‘I have given three years to the NHS as an IMG – but it isn’t enough for GP training’
items.summary: Dr Gauri Sathe shares her experience as an IMG who has worked in the NHS, but has been unable to get a place for GP training due to the medical specialty training prioritisation bill When I came to this country as an international medical graduate (IMG) I knew I would have to prove myself.

items.title: ICN calls for greater investment in primary care nurses
items.summary: Governments should invest in primary care nurses and allow them to form the frontline in the fight against non-communicable diseases (NCDs), the International Council of Nurses (ICN) has said.

items.title: GP practice to reopen after more than four years following Government-funded upgrades
items.summary: A GP practice that closed in 2022 will reopen next year following Government-funded refurbishments to its premises. Griffin Close Surgery in Frizington, Cumbria, received more than £366,000 from NHS England’s Primary Care Utilisation and Modernisation Fund (UMF).

items.title: Physical activity may improve quality of life during menopause
items.summary: Physical activity can raise mood levels and improve overall quality of life for women during menopause, a study has found.

items.title: GPs should have ‘clear escalation routes’ for raising A&G safety concerns, says NHSE
items.summary: GP practices should have ‘clear escalation routes’ for raising safety concerns and report when advice and guidance (A&G) responses from hospitals are ‘delayed or unclear’, NHS England has said in new guidance.

items.title: NMC’s executive director of professional regulation to step down
items.summary: The executive director of professional regulation at the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) is stepping down after four years. Lesley Maslen will be succeeded by Richard Cartland at the end of November on a temporary basis while recruitment for a permanent position takes place.

items.title: Two thirds of patients incorrectly contact GP about other NHS services, RCGP warns
items.summary: Almost two thirds of patients contact their GP because they are were waiting for care from another NHS service, according to a new RCGP survey. The college said this was adding to the ‘avoidable workload’ for GPs and increasing anxiety for patients.

items.title: HPV vaccination before pregnancy linked with reduced preterm birth
items.summary: A study has found benefits of HPV vaccination that extend beyond cancer prevention to reduced risk of adverse outcomes in pregnancy. The Swedish analysis showed having a human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine before pregnancy is associated with a lower risk of major pregnancy complications including preterm birth.

items.title: ‘Are we robbing GP Peter to pay Pharmacist Paul?’
items.summary: Dr David Salkin asks whether competition in flu vaccination highlights the need for a level playing field for general practice Well it’s that time of year again. Flu vaccinations are upon us, and nothing creates a fever and chills more than the rush to vaccinate as many of the practice population as possible.

items.title: Menopause supplements an overpriced ‘wild west’, analysis finds
items.summary: Many supplements marketed at perimenopausal and menopausal women are severely overpriced and lack meaningful doses of recommended nutrients, an analysis by Which? has found.

items.title: Wound scanning app helping to ‘save nurse time’
items.summary: A wound-scanning app used by district nursing teams in Wales has helped save nurse time and improve patient care. The ‘Minuteful for Wound’ app, developed by technology company Precision Health Tech, allows nurses and healthcare staff to scan and measure wounds so they can be monitored virtually.

items.title: Frontline doctors demand ‘independent review’ of GP list-cleansing drive
items.summary: The Doctors’ Association UK has called for an independent review into NHS England’s GP list-cleansing drive, warning that practices are suffering ‘sudden and destabilising’ reductions in funding because of the administrative exercise.
